---
title: "Value Added v2.2 candidates"
subtitle: "Pupils' ethnicity and neighbourhood deprivation, tested for every group of pupils and every year: what they add, what they change, and the case for and against."
---

```{r setup}
#| include: false
source(here::here("R", "site_helpers.R"))
X <- readRDS(here::here("data", "v22_candidates.rds"))
C <- X$comparison |> group_by(group) |>
  mutate(daic = aic - aic[spec == "v2.1"], drmse = 100 * (rmse_oos / rmse_oos[spec == "v2.1"] - 1)) |> ungroup()
cv <- function(g, s, col) C[[col]][C$group == g & C$spec == s]
pe <- function(b) 100 * (exp(b) - 1)
gs <- function(g, q, col) X$gain_summary[[col]][X$gain_summary$group == g & X$gain_summary$eth_q == q]
gr <- function(g, r) X$gain_region$change[X$gain_region$group == g & X$gain_region$gor_name == r]
GL <- GROUP_LABELS
SPEC_COL <- c(eth = DPURPLE, dep = BLUE, both = MPURPLE)
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Candidates, not changes

Value Added v2.1 is what this site publishes. This page tests two
candidate terms for a v2.2, the way the [v2.1 candidates](method.qmd#sec-v21)
were tested: on identical school-years, for every group, with each year
held out in turn. Where the terms came from is set out in the
[neighbourhood covariates experiment](neighbourhood_covariates.qmd).
:::

::: {.callout-important}
## In short

- **Neighbourhood deprivation** helps every group, in every year. It
  improves predictions out of sample for all five groups and takes about
  `r sprintf("%.0f", min(-C$la_var_change[C$spec == "dep" & C$group != "disadvantaged"]))` to
  `r sprintf("%.0f", max(-C$la_var_change[C$spec == "dep" & C$group != "disadvantaged"]))`% off
  the local authority variance (`r sprintf("%.0f", -cv("disadvantaged", "dep", "la_var_change"))`%
  for disadvantaged pupils). It changes little else. **Recommended for v2.2.**
- **Pupils' ethnicity** matters almost only for disadvantaged pupils.
  There it is a large gain
  (AIC `r sprintf("%.0f", cv("disadvantaged", "eth", "daic"))`). For
  non-disadvantaged pupils it is zero. A third of schools would change
  fifth on disadvantaged value added, with London losing most. Whether
  to adjust for it is a question of what value added is for. **Recommended
  beside v2.2, not in it**, as v2.1 publishes the kind of absence.
:::

## The candidates {#sec-terms}

| Term | What it is | Source | One standard deviation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pupils' ethnicity | The school's share of White British pupils, each January | School census, 2022 to 2025 | `r sprintf("%.0f", X$term_sd[["z_eth"]])` percentage points |
| Neighbourhood deprivation | Share of households deprived in two or more of four dimensions (employment, education, health, housing), over the 150 Output Areas nearest the school | Census 2021, TS011 | `r sprintf("%.1f", X$term_sd[["z_dep"]])` percentage points |

v2.1 has neither. It has English as an additional language for pupils.
For the neighbourhood it has adult qualifications only. Ethnicity is
matched to `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * X$eth_coverage)`% of school-years, by
year.

## Fit and prediction {#sec-fit}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-fit
#| tbl-cap: "Each candidate against v2.1, by group: the effect of one standard deviation (% of Attainment 8), the change in AIC (negative is better), and the change in out-of-sample error (each year predicted from the other three, averaged)."
C |> filter(spec != "v2.1") |>
  mutate(g = factor(group, names(GL)), s = factor(spec, c("eth", "dep", "both"))) |> arrange(g, s) |>
  transmute(Group = GL[group], Candidate = X$labels[spec],
            Ethnicity = ifelse(is.na(b_eth), "", sprintf("%+.1f%%", pe(b_eth))),
            Deprivation = ifelse(is.na(b_dep), "", sprintf("%+.1f%%", pe(b_dep))),
            `AIC change` = sprintf("%.0f", daic), `Out-of-sample error` = sprintf("%+.2f%%", drmse)) |>
  kt(align = "llrrrr") |> kableExtra::collapse_rows(columns = 1, valign = "top")
```

Both terms improve fit and prediction for every group, with one
exception: ethnicity does nothing for non-disadvantaged pupils
(`r sprintf("%+.1f%%", pe(cv("non_disadvantaged", "eth", "b_eth")))`, AIC
`r sprintf("%.0f", cv("non_disadvantaged", "eth", "daic"))`). For
disadvantaged pupils, a school with one standard deviation more White
British pupils gets `r sprintf("%.1f%%", -pe(cv("disadvantaged", "eth", "b_eth")))`
lower Attainment 8 for its disadvantaged pupils, all else in v2.1 equal.
That matches what is well known at pupil level: disadvantaged White
British pupils do less well at GCSE than disadvantaged pupils of most
other ethnic groups. Neighbourhood deprivation goes the other way, about
`r sprintf("%+.0f%%", pe(cv("all", "dep", "b_dep")))` per standard deviation for most groups. At the same share
of graduates, a school among more deprived households does a little
better than v2.1 expects.

## Year by year {#sec-years}

```{r}
#| label: fig-years
#| fig-cap: "Each term's effect fitted on each year alone (both terms together, with v2.1's terms and region/local authority effects), % of Attainment 8 per standard deviation, with 95% intervals."
#| fig-height: 5.2
yd <- X$yearly |> mutate(term = ifelse(term == "z_eth", "Pupils' ethnicity (White British share)", "Neighbourhood deprivation"),
                          grp = factor(GL[group], GL))
ggplot(yd, aes(year, pct, colour = grp, group = grp)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = GREY) +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), position = position_dodge(width = 0.5), linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_line(position = position_dodge(width = 0.5), linewidth = 0.6, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_point(position = position_dodge(width = 0.5), size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~ term) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = GROUP_COL, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "% of Attainment 8 per SD") + theme_note(11)
```

Both are steady. Ethnicity is between −4% and −6.5% for disadvantaged
pupils every year and near zero for non-disadvantaged pupils every year.
Deprivation is positive in every year for every group, largest in
2024/25.

## What would move {#sec-moves}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-moves
#| tbl-cap: "What each candidate changes against v2.1: the correlation of schools' value added, the share that change fifth, the average change in a school's value added (Attainment 8 points), the correlation of local authority effects, the change in local authority variance, and Brighton and Hove."
C |> filter(spec != "v2.1") |>
  mutate(g = factor(group, names(GL)), s = factor(spec, c("eth", "dep", "both"))) |> arrange(g, s) |>
  transmute(Group = GL[group], Candidate = X$labels[spec],
            `Schools: r` = sprintf("%.3f", r_school), `Change fifth` = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * moved_quintile),
            `Average change` = sprintf("%.2f", mean_abs_change), `Authorities: r` = sprintf("%.3f", r_la),
            `Authority variance` = sprintf("%+.0f%%", la_var_change),
            `Brighton and Hove` = sprintf("%+.1f%% (%s)", bh_effect, ord(bh_rank))) |>
  kt(align = "llrrrrrr") |> kableExtra::collapse_rows(columns = 1, valign = "top")
```

Neighbourhood deprivation is a light touch. Schools' value added
correlates at `r sprintf("%.3f", cv("all", "dep", "r_school"))` with v2.1
for all pupils, and the average school moves by
`r sprintf("%.2f", cv("all", "dep", "mean_abs_change"))` points. It
lowers graduate-rich, deprived places' effects: Brighton and Hove goes
from `r sprintf("%+.1f%%", cv("all", "v2.1", "bh_effect"))` to
`r sprintf("%+.1f%%", cv("all", "dep", "bh_effect"))` for all pupils.

Ethnicity is not a light touch for disadvantaged pupils.
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * cv("disadvantaged", "eth", "moved_quintile"))` of
schools change fifth, and the average school's disadvantaged value added
moves by `r sprintf("%.1f", cv("disadvantaged", "eth", "mean_abs_change"))`
points.

## Who would gain and who would lose {#sec-who}

```{r}
#| label: fig-who
#| fig-cap: "The average change in schools' value added (Attainment 8 points) with both terms added, by fifth of schools on their share of White British pupils, for each group."
#| fig-height: 3.8
wd <- X$gain_summary |> group_by(eth_q) |> mutate(lab = sprintf("Fifth %d\n(%.0f%% WB)", eth_q, mean(wbri))) |> ungroup() |>
  mutate(grp = factor(GL[group], GL))
ggplot(wd, aes(lab, change, fill = grp)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = GREY) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.75) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = GROUP_COL, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Schools by share of White British pupils (fifths)", y = "Change in value added (points)") + theme_note(11)
```

With both terms, disadvantaged value added falls by
`r sprintf("%.1f", -gs("disadvantaged", 1, "change"))` points on average in
the fifth of schools with the fewest White British pupils (about
`r sprintf("%.0f", gs("disadvantaged", 1, "wbri"))`%), and rises by up to
`r sprintf("%.1f", max(X$gain_summary$change[X$gain_summary$group == "disadvantaged"]))` in
the middle and upper fifths. By region, London's schools lose
`r sprintf("%.1f", -gr("disadvantaged", "London"))` points of disadvantaged
value added on average; every other region gains a little, except the
West Midlands (`r sprintf("%+.1f", gr("disadvantaged", "West Midlands"))`).

## The case for and against ethnicity {#sec-case}

**For.** Value added is meant to compare schools fairly, on what they do
rather than whom they teach. Disadvantaged White British pupils do less
well wherever they are taught. A school that serves many of them is
judged against schools whose disadvantaged pupils were always more
likely to do well. Adjusting for it is what DfE's contextual value added
did until 2011. It is also what the evidence here supports, for this
group, in every year.

**Against.** An expectation that varies by ethnicity builds a lower
expectation into the measure for some pupils. That was the main
criticism of contextual value added and part of why it was dropped. It
would also take out of view a real gap that policy should see: the
low attainment of disadvantaged White British pupils. And the term is a
school share, not each pupil's own ethnicity, so it adjusts schools, not
pupils.

**What we would do.** Publish it beside v2.2 rather than in it, as v2.1
publishes value added allowing for the kind of absence. The headline
measure stays free of ethnicity. Anyone asking "how does this school do
with its particular disadvantaged pupils?" can see the answer next to it.

## What we would recommend for v2.2 {#sec-recommend}

::: {.callout-tip}
This approach is agreed and on the [roadmap](roadmap.qmd) for a future
release. Until then, everything on this site is Value Added v2.1.
:::

1. **Add neighbourhood deprivation to the expectation**, beside
   neighbourhood education. It is a neighbourhood measure, like the term
   it sits next to. It helps every group in every year. It makes the
   neighbourhood term fairer to places with many graduates and many
   deprived households.
2. **Publish value added allowing for pupils' ethnicity beside the
   headline**, for every group, labelled, with this page as its
   explanation.
3. **Keep testing**: whether the ethnicity effect is a White British
   effect or varies by group (Gypsy, Roma and Traveller, Black Caribbean
   and others), using the census's detailed shares.
